info.bio: Ann Delia Derbyshire (seudónimos: Harper Russe/ Li de la Russe/Li de la Red/ Doris Hays) 1937-2001. Nació el 5 de mayo de 1937 en Coventry, Inglaterra. Compositora de música concreta, pionera en el ámbito de la música electrónica, escultora sonora; experimentó con diversos sonidos para el medio radiofónico, televisivo, el teatro y el cine. Sus trabajos más conocidos son: el tema musical realizado para la serie británica de ciencia ficción

scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Tras el éxito de los Beatles, las cuatro grandes discográficas (EMI, Decca, Pye y Philips) saquearon metódicamente las provincias: firmaban barato y esperaban a ver qué pegaba. Pye, del veterano Louis Benjamin, tenía a los Kinks y a los Searchers y fama de contratos miserables. Los Ugly’s de Birmingham, nacidos del skiffle y curtidos en los clubes alemanes, se distinguían por su conciencia social; la cara B de su tercer single, «A Quiet Explosion» (21 de enero de 1966), con órgano Vox Continental, un riff con eco a lo Delia Derbyshire y un bajo descendente que es la bomba cayendo, desapareció en la sobreproducción del momento, pero es un disco extraño y auténtico que se acerca a la psicodelia. A principios de 1966 las bases del beat y del R&B se llevaron al límite, como bajo una enorme presión: «Keep on Running» de Spencer Davis casa soul y mod pop, los Wheels de Belfast aceleran sin freno en «Bad Little Woman» y los Poets de Glasgow, de Andrew Loog Oldham, desquician el «Baby Don’t You Do It» de Marvin Gaye.

podcast.title: Joining the BBC Radiophonic Workshop (1960)
podcast.body: In 1960, Delia Derbyshire joined the BBC, initially as an assistant, a position that underutilized her Cambridge education in mathematics and acoustics. She eventually managed to secure a transfer to the BBC Radiophonic Workshop, a pioneering project established in 1958 to experiment with creating music using electricity, after a significant struggle to be allowed to work there. "Delia Derbyshire en 1960 entra a trabajar en la BBC y se da cuenta de que en la BBC hay un proyecto que había fundado un par de años antes de la BBC, en el 58 que se llama de Radiophonic Workshop."

srcs.episode: Cómo una mujer inventó la música electrónica ⧸ Delia Derbyshire

podcast.title: BBC Radiophonic Workshop Tenure (1962-1973)
podcast.body: Delia Derbyshire joined the BBC Radiophonic Workshop in 1962, a facility that Daphne Oram had helped establish. She remained there for 11 years, during which she worked on electronic music for nearly 200 radio and television programs, becoming a pivotal figure in the history of electronic music. "She stayed for 11 years, working on electronic music for close to 200 radio and TV programs using tape machines and oscillators and sine wave generators."

podcast.title: Experimental Compositions (1962-1975)
podcast.body: Delia Derbyshire continued her work on experimental compositions until 1975. Her contributions to electronic music, utilizing a variety of available equipment like tape machines, oscillators, and sine wave generators, are considered very important in the genre's history. "This is very important stuff in the history of electronic music, and she continued with her experimental compositions until 1975."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Hidden Figures

podcast.title: "Doctor Who" Theme Arrangement (1963-1980)
podcast.body: Delia Derbyshire's most famous work is her electronic arrangement of the "Doctor Who" theme. While composer Ron Granger wrote the original tune, Derbyshire was responsible for giving it its familiar and iconic electronic sound, which viewers heard from 1963 through 1980. Her reinterpretation is considered one of the most famous pieces of sci-fi music in the universe. "Her most famous work involved taking the theme from the BBC show Dr. Who and turning it into something entirely electronic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Hidden Figures

podcast.title: Post-1970 Experimental Career
podcast.body: After 1970, Delia Derbyshire's work remained highly experimental, with her continuing to create thousands of electronic sound effects for films, series, and advertisements. She also gave pioneering live performances of electronic music in experimental theaters at a time when dedicated electronic music albums were virtually non-existent. "Ella hizo miles de zenas de miles de efectos de sonidos electrónicos que se utilizaron en películas en series en anuncios en un montón de cosas."

podcast.title: Absolute Mother of Electronic Music
podcast.body: Delia Derbyshire is regarded as the absolute mother of electronic music, pioneering the genre as we know it today. She laid the foundational concepts for modern electronic music through her innovative work with pre-recorded sounds and sequencing. "madre absoluta de la música electrónica."

podcast.body: Delia Derbyshire joined the BBC Radiophonic Workshop in 1962 and remained there for 11 years, contributing to electronic music for nearly 200 radio and television programs, employing tape machines, oscillators, and sine wave generators. She continued her experimental compositions until 1975, making significant contributions to the history of electronic music. "She stayed for 11 years, working on electronic music for close to 200 radio and TV programs using tape machines and oscillators and sine wave generators."

srcs.episode: Hidden Figures

podcast.title: Delayed Recognition and Financial Injustice
podcast.body: For many years, Delia Derbyshire remained an overlooked figure, never appearing in the credits for the "Doctor Who Theme" or receiving any payment for her contributions. While her work garnered significant enthusiasm in 1965 and 1966, it was only many years later that efforts began to acknowledge her legacy and credit her properly, though tragically, much of her work was lost due to this initial neglect. "nunca apareció en los créditos de la banda sonada del Dr. Juni de la serie ni de ningún lado, y nunca recibió ni dinero, y nunca recibió nada por lo que hizo."

srcs.episode: Cómo una mujer inventó la música electrónica ⧸ Delia Derbyshire

podcast.title: Discrimination at Decca Records
podcast.body: Despite her advanced education in mathematics and music, Delia Derbyshire faced significant gender discrimination in the professional world. She was rejected by Decca Records, one of the most important record labels of the era, because their company policy prohibited hiring women for engineering or sound production roles, limiting their employment to cleaning or assistant positions. "no la contrataron porque por política de empresa en deca recorso no contrataban a mujeres ni en ingeniería ni en producción de sonidos."

srcs.episode: Cómo una mujer inventó la música electrónica ⧸ Delia Derbyshire

podcast.title: Early Career Struggles
podcast.body: After graduating, Delia Derbyshire initially struggled to find work in her field due to her gender. She ended up giving private lessons to wealthy children in mathematics and other subjects, and also worked as an assistant for an important music distributor, a role far beneath her qualifications. "acabó, pues hagas la pobre dando clases a niños ricos."

srcs.episode: Cómo una mujer inventó la música electrónica ⧸ Delia Derbyshire

podcast.title: Early Life and Education
podcast.body: Delia Derbyshire was born in the United Kingdom between the two World Wars. She was exceptionally intelligent, a trait that allowed her to attend Cambridge University, one of the world's leading institutions, at a time when very few women had such opportunities. She studied mathematics and music, and conducted experimental work in acoustics and electricity. "Nace en el rinonido justo entre las dos guerras mundiales."

srcs.episode: Cómo una mujer inventó la música electrónica ⧸ Delia Derbyshire

podcast.title: Electronic Music Pioneer at BBC Radiofonc Workshop
podcast.body: Delia Derbyshire worked at the BBC Radiofonc Workshop for 11 years, starting in 1962. During her tenure, she composed electronic music for nearly 200 radio and TV programs, utilizing tape machines, oscillators, and sine wave generators in her experimental compositions until 1975, making significant contributions to the field. "She stayed there for 11 years, working on electronic music for close to 200 radio and TV programs, using tape machines and oscillators and sine wave generators, whatever she could get her hands on."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Unsung Heroines

podcast.title: Iconic "Doctor Who" Theme Arrangement
podcast.body: Her most famous work is the electronic arrangement of the theme song for the BBC show "Dr. Who." Although the music was written by composer Ron Grainer, Delia Derbyshire transformed it into its familiar electronic sound, which was heard by viewers at the start of every episode from 1963 to 1980, making it one of the most famous TV theme songs ever. "But she is the one who gave it that familiar electronic arrangement."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Unsung Heroines

podcast.title: Lack of Recognition for Doctor Who Theme
podcast.body: Despite her instrumental role in composing the groundbreaking 100% electronic "Doctor Who Theme" in 1963, Delia Derbyshire received no credit for her work. Ron Grainer, who provided only basic melodies, was the sole person credited initially and received all the financial compensation. Her immense contribution remained unrecognized for many years, highlighting a profound injustice. "Y nadie se lo reconoció ni siquiera salía en los créditos de la película."

srcs.episode: Cómo una mujer inventó la música electrónica ⧸ Delia Derbyshire

podcast.title: Legacy Recovery and Documentation
podcast.body: In recent years, there has been a significant effort to recover and recognize Delia Derbyshire's legacy. A documentary has been made about her life and work, and an official website dedicated to her provides a comprehensive biography. However, due to the historical lack of recognition, much of her pioneering work and information has unfortunately been lost. "En los últimos años sí que se ha intentado recuperar un poco el legado de lo que fue de Adervisari y se ha hecho el buen documental..."

srcs.episode: Cómo una mujer inventó la música electrónica ⧸ Delia Derbyshire

podcast.title: No Reconocimiento en Créditos de Dr. Who (Años 60)
podcast.body: A principios de los años 60, Delia Derbyshire recibió el encargo de componer la música para una nueva serie, Dr. Who. La sintonía resultante fue un hito crucial para la aceptación y popularización de la música electrónica. Sin embargo, su significativa contribución a la composición nunca fue reconocida en los créditos de la canción, a pesar de su rol pionero en los estudios de la BBC Radiofonic Workshop. "Sin embargo, su contribución nunca fue reconocida en los créditos de la canción."

srcs.episode: Ellas vieron el futuro: Pioneras de la música electrónica

podcast.title: Pioneering Electronic Music Techniques
podcast.body: While working at the Radiophonic Workshop, Delia Derbyshire revolutionized music by using pre-recorded sounds as musical notes and developing sequencing techniques. This groundbreaking approach laid the conceptual groundwork for modern electronic music, though the speaker notes that sequencing in a basic form might have existed slightly earlier. "Esta mujer está utilizando sonidos pregravados como notas y está secuenciendo, está creando secuenciación, con lo cual esta mujer está dando las bases de lo que luego más adelante sería la electrónica moderna."
